reference: Numerics @ 2a0357a. Runs corehydro::numerics::support::run_callback (core/include/corehydro/numerics/support/callback_runner.hpp), group "bootstrap", method "run", against the four delegates named by `construct.callback` (the resample), `construct.fit`, `construct.statistic` and `construct.jackknife` -- each a function the four runners write themselves as a native closure (a C++ lambda, an R closure, a Python function, a C# delegate), so every case crosses the real host-language boundary four ways. This is upstream's OWN API: Bootstrap<TData> exposes ResampleFunction, FitFunction, StatisticFunction and JackknifeFunction as public properties and a C# caller supplies all of them; the model registry under sampling/bootstrap/ that the `bootstrap` kind drives is corehydro fixture scaffolding, and until this group existed the packages could reach the bootstrap only through it. EVERY expected value here is EMITTER-READ: no upstream test bootstraps this model, so the oracle is the real Numerics Bootstrap driven by tools/oracle_emitter with the equivalent C# delegates, never a value computed by this repo's own C++. Every catalog callback is built from + - * / and comparisons alone, with the summation written as an explicit loop rather than any language's sum(), mean() or Average(): R's sum() and mean() accumulate in extended precision where C++, Python and C# accumulate in double, and one differing bit in a fitted mean moves a percentile. The result layout (replicates / failed_replicates / alpha, then statistic[i] with its five companions, then parameter[j] with the same, and dims = {n_statistics, n_parameters}) is documented in core/include/corehydro/numerics/support/callback/bootstrap.hpp; the `named` assertions below read it by label rather than by an index that shifts with the statistic count.

callbacks.Resample_Iid: resample(data, parameters, prng) -> n draws of data[prng.Next(0, n)], n = data.Length  [corehydro addition, upstream's Func<TData, ParameterSet, Random, TData> shape: the ordinary nonparametric bootstrap resample, drawing every index off the generator the replicate hands in -- which is the property the RNG handle exists for. The index is 0-based, as the ported MersenneTwister.Next(minInclusive, maxExclusive) is]
callbacks.Fit_Mean: fit(data) -> [sum(data) / data.Length], summed in an explicit loop  [corehydro addition, upstream's Func<TData, ParameterSet> shape: a one-parameter model whose fit is the sample mean]
callbacks.Stat_Identity: statistic(parameters) -> parameters  [corehydro addition, upstream's Func<ParameterSet, double[]> shape: the statistic IS the fitted parameter, so the interval is an interval on the mean]
callbacks.Stat_MeanAndSquare: statistic(parameters) -> [p0, p0 * p0]  [corehydro addition: two statistics rather than one, so the per-statistic layout and the second statistic's own interval are pinned]
callbacks.Jack_LeaveOneOut: jackknife(data, index) -> data without element `index`, counting from 0  [corehydro addition, upstream's Func<TData, int, TData> shape: the leave-one-out sample ComputeAccelerationConstants needs for BCa]
